title: Model choice & tuning sprint — customer chronicle
body:
Context:
Customer: mid-market commerce platform. Main ask: chat+retrieval assistant to answer product and order questions for internal ops (not public web). Data: sanitized product catalog + anonymized orders; PII redaction required.
Goals / Acceptance criteria for POC:
- Functional: >= 85% answer accuracy on the 120-case gold set (operator-labeled).
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms for short queries (avg tokens generated < 90) when pinned to dedicated capacity in us-west.
- Cost target: <= $1200 / month equivalent at 100k queries/mo (ballpark; used for tradeoffs).
- Safety: no PII leakage in top-1 results.
- Ops: ability to swap model variant without code changes; automated fallback on overload.
Constraints / Environment:
- Customer will deploy on a Dedicated pool (NVIDIA H100 equivalent).
- Network: VPC, egress restricted. Cannot use external hosted embeddings service.
- Storage: catalog snapshot ~4GB, retrieval via FAISS on local NVMe.
- Sequence distribution: median prompt 80 tokens, generated tokens median 60, 95th gen length 320.
Shortlist rationale (models we tested / will test):
1) Mistral-7B-v1 (base) — strong instruction-following for short form; good latency and low memory. Candidate for q4_0 / q4_k_m benchmark.
2) Falcon-40B-instruct (server variant) — higher quality on complex multi-hop operator queries; heavy but hit budget if used only for 1% of traffic as fallback.
3) Llama-2-13B (opt-variant) — middle ground; supports 4-bit quant with acceptable quality drop; good baseline for cost vs quality.
4) RedModel-3B-lite (customer-specific small model for ultra-low-latency checks) — to route quick factual lookups.
Quantization profiles considered:
- q4_0: fastest, smaller memory, some arithmetic noise on factuals.
- q4_k_m / q4_f16 (mixed): better fidelity for weights affecting generation quality; slightly higher mem and latency.
- awq-q3b: experimental — extremely low mem, riskier for commonsense reasoning.
Experiment matrix (primary axes):
- model: {Mistral-7B, Llama-2-13B, Falcon-40B-fallback, RedModel-3B}
- quant: {fp16, q4_0, q4_k_m}
- batch size (inference): {1, 4, 8} — observe p95 latency trade-offs
- kv-cache policy: {full, prefix-cached 256-token}
- prompt-template style: {direct-instruction, few-shot, retrieval-augmented + instructions}
- reranker: {none, lightweight cross-encoder rerank on top-5}
Metrics to capture per run (schema for the bench sheet):
- latency: p50, p90, p95, p99 (ms)
- throughput: tokens/sec at steady state
- memory: peak GPU memory (GB)
- unit cost: tokens-equivalent USD (est)
- quality: accuracy on gold set (%), hallucination rate (manual sampling %), answer faithfulness (0-1)
- failure modes: OOM, truncation, broken JSON outputs
Recommended initial experiments (week 0–1):
- Baseline: Mistral-7B fp16 batch=1, kv=full, direct instruction prompt. Collect latency and accuracy.
- Quant sweep: Mistral-7B q4_0 and q4_k_m, same prompt. Compare accuracy delta and p95 change.
- Mixed routing: Llama-13B q4_k_m for 90% traffic, Falcon-40B fp16 as 10% fallback for low-confidence queries (conf threshold 0.6). Measure per-query latency and end-to-end p95.
Prompt & pipeline tuning notes:
- Use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): short catalog snippets appended (≤3 docs, heuristics to avoid PII).
- Template structure (kept minimal): system instruction -> retrieved facts -> operator question -> expected output format (JSON or bullet).
- Reranking helps reduce hallucination; we saw 12–18% fewer hallucinations in small internal tests when using a light cross-encoder reranker on top-5 retrievals.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated system + retrieval combos; cache TTL 10m for ops workload.
- Tokenization sanity: ensure tokenizer consistent across quant variant; small differences in token boundaries caused +3–4% variance in ROUGE-like metrics in previous POC.
Quality evaluation plan:
- 120-case gold set: 60 factual readoffs (catalog lookups), 40 multi-step operational Qs, 20 edge/legal phrasing. Binary correctness + short rubric.
- Crowd sanity checks: 50 sampled responses via internal reviewers focusing on hallucination and PII.
- Regression harness: store prompt-response pairs and run diff against base (Mistral fp16) daily during tuning runs.
Runbook / rollout steps (can be scripted):
1) Start Mistral-7B fp16 on dedicated pool; warmup with 2000 synthetic queries.
2) Enable q4_0 bench variant in A/B route (5% traffic) with metrics pipeline in place. Monitor error budget and accuracy.
3) If accuracy drop <= 4% and lat p95 improves >= 10%, expand q4_0 to 30%. Else revert.
4) Add reranker in pipeline; run controlled 10%->50% ramp to measure hallucination reductions.
5) Add fallback Falcon-40B route for low-confidence queries (model confidence heuristic + retrieval mismatch).
Operational considerations / gotchas:
- Quantized models can show non-linear failure modes on long sequences (≥200 tokens). Test extremes explicitly.
- When using prefix KV caching, eviction behavior on restarts caused stale context in one customer test — add instrumentation on cache hits/misses.
- For on-prem Dedicated pools, ensure driver/kernel versions match the quant runtime (we saw incompat issues with one H100 kernel a few quarters ago).
- Measure cold-starts: model loads for q4 variants are faster but still hit 1.2–1.8s cold start; account for scaling policy.
Open questions / decision points for customer workshop:
- Are we comfortable with a 3–5% quality regression in q4_0 if it buys 30–40% latency improvement? Customer ops prefers faster responses for high-frequency simple queries.
- Fallback SLA: how many forced escalations to the large model (Falcon-40B) monthly is acceptable for cost?
- PII handling: do we keep a redaction pre-filter or rely on model output filtering? Recommendation: both — pre-filter + output checks.
Milestones & timeline (4-week sprint):
- Week 1: baseline runs + quant sweep + gold-set initial eval.
- Week 2: implement reranker + caching + door-to-door smoke tests in dedicated env.
- Week 3: mixed routing experiments + fallback config + cost modeling.
- Week 4: customer workshop demo + decision memo and recommended production config.
Appendices (quick notes):
- Quick CLI snippet to run bench (internal runner): redwood-bench run --model mistral-7b --quant q4_0 --batch 1 --seq 256 --out results/mist-q4.json
- Quick health check metrics to ship: p95_latency, gold_accuracy, hallucination_sample_rate, avg_gpu_mem
- Immediate TODOs:
  - [ ] Create gold-set labeling doc and share with customer (Sofia) — due 2025-11-18.
  - [ ] Schedule kernel/version validation with infra (Liam) — due 2025-11-14.
  - [ ] Implement lightweight reranker (Priya) prototype and instrument metrics — due 2025-11-22.
Notes to future self: capture narrative of any counterintuitive failures (quant X + reranker Y) — those are gold for playbook.

-- end of chronicle --
